targets.authors: Soroka, S., Fournier, P., & Nir, L.
targets.title: Cross‐national evidence of a negativity bias in psychophysiological reactions to news.
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, we set out to directly replicate one of the two central findings of SFN. We preregistered that we expect that negative news compared to positive news increases skin conductance levels (SCLs) as an indicator of arousal (H1).
targets.outcome_quote: To summarise, our results for SCL should be seen as in line with SFN’s results.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly judge the replicated SCL finding in line with the original despite smaller nonsignificant effects. The self-reported arousal and valence tests are extensions that the original did not measure; the heart-rate attention finding was explicitly not replicated.

reasoning: New Netherlands sample retests the 2019 SCL result. The earlier 2015 pilot is background in the chain, not the target. Correct publisher PDF identity verified; OpenAlex PDF URL was not used because its article identifier differed.
